messages.subject: choosing K and Gen
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a 20 generation AIL chicken population, where 60 founders(F0) are sequenced to 30X and every offspring from F2-F20 are sequenced to about 0.5X. I am thinking about running STITCH with reference haplotype mode(Phase F0 and plug in it as ref).  could you please offer me some advice in choosing K and nGen?

Thank you very much.
Best,
Yanjun

messages.subject: Re: choosing K and Gen
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yanjun,

I would try a range of K, say 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30, over a small interval, like 5 Mbp or even a chromosome, and check results against either
1) known results (if you sequenced some of the F2 to F20 to higher coverage or have array results)
2) by holding out and sub-sampling some of the founders (e.g. use 55 founders at 30X, downsample 5 founders to 0.5X, include them as offspring and compare imputation results to truth)
3) compare info score distributions from the different K and choose the one with the highest average

STITCH should be fairly robust to nGen, which just bounds recombination rate (default expected value 0.5 cM / Mb). I would set nGen = 10 based on your situation. Brief googling suggests chicken recombination rate should be ~3 cM / Mb
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2661806/
https://www.ensembl.org/Gallus_gallus/Info/Annotation
so you may want to set "expRate" to 3

Finally although hopefully you will get good results with STITCH here, in case you were not already considering it, given the nature of the analysis population (deeply sequenced founders and pedigrees available vs. random unrelated individuals from a randomly mating population), alternative imputation methods may yield more satisfactory results e.g. AlphaImpute, FImpute, Findhap, etc.

Best wishes,
Robbie

messages.subject: Re: choosing K and Gen
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Robert,

I am running into a issue with the validate_reference_legend function. I plugged in a legend file that have info on all chromosomes.  Based on the code you posed on github(copied as it is below), I troubleshoot the probelm to -- the same position(in bp) from different chromosome have the same ref/alt allele, for example  CM000104.4-10002514 10002514 G A and CM000110.4-10002514 10002514 G A, and the verifying is not chromosome based.

I am a little bit worried about this, does this mean that the chromosome is not verified when loading the legend?  Should I split the legend and hap file based on chromosome beforehand?

Thank you again for taking your time.

Best,
Yanjun

legend_snps <- paste(
legend[, "position"], legend[,"a0"], legend[, "a1"],
sep = "-"
)
t <- table(legend_snps)
if (sum(t > 1) > 0) {
## argh R - get character not factor
m <- match(names(t[t>1])[1], legend_snps)
example <- sapply(
legend[m, c("position", "a0", "a1")],
as.character
)
stop(
paste0(
"There are ", sum(t > 1), " duplicate row ids. ",
"One such example is ",
paste0(example, collapse = " ")
)
)

messages.subject: Re: choosing K and Gen
messages.body_plain:
Hi Zan,

Hmm, good point. The chromosome is not verified when loading the legend. I used an IMPUTE2 style legend file, which does not have an explicit chromosome argument. You are right in that the 4th column of ID can and should be checked for; in your case, this would have caught the problem (non-uniqueness with respect to position, ref and alt).

I do not intend to introduce a chromosome column to maintain compatibility with IMPUTE2 reference format, so I suggest you break your files by chromosome, but I will add in a check with an error message to make this clearer in the future.

Thanks for reporting this,
Best,
Robbie

messages.subject: STITCH 1.3.7 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am releasing STITCH 1.3.7, which does the following

1. Misc changes to reduce RAM usage

2. Standardize messaging and change to stderr vs stdout (much easier to read messaging of what happens when)

3. Re-enable printing of r2 oriented for major allele during progression (somehow I disabled orienting for major allele a long time ago and never re-enabled it - regardless, use external tools to validate imputation performance, the r2 that is printed per-iteration is intended primarily to help decide how many iterations are sufficient for imputation)

4. More errors and checking for reference legend file (the reference legend file is in IMPUTE2 format, which does not specify chromosome, so an error is now thrown if the position the SNPs are given in ever decreases, like would happen if results from more than one chromosome were contained in the same file)

https://github.com/rwdavies/STITCH

Best,

Robbie
